name: New Democracy
summary: New Democracy is Mao Zedong's theory that the revolution in a colonial, semi-colonial and semi-feudal country must pass through a democratic stage before socialism. The stage is a joint dictatorship of the revolutionary classes (workers, peasants, petty and national bourgeoisie) led by the working class, with land to the tiller, state ownership of big banks and monopolistic enterprises, protection of non-monopoly private capital, and a national, scientific and mass culture.
scope: Mao Zedong's theory as set out in On New Democracy (1940) and On Coalition Government (1945), as the programme of the Chinese Communist Party for the democratic stage of the revolution. It does not cover later Maoist doctrine (continuing revolution, the Cultural Revolution), the socialist stage, or other parties named New Democracy.

notes: Answers rest on Mao's 1940 essay and 1945 report; the later record of the People's Republic is not used. Themes searched in the two texts: economy (ownership, land, tax, labour), government (suffrage, parties, assembly, army), liberty (speech, religion), society (women, minorities, culture), world (imperialism, Soviet Union, UN) and means (revolution, armed struggle, alliances). Ecology, technology and most culture-war and moral statements are not addressed and stay null.
